content: Kodi InfoTag migration, verified against xbmc/xbmc master source. xbmc.python addon version per release (raw addons/xbmc.python/addon.xml): 19.5-Matrix = 3.0.0, 20.5-Nexus = 3.0.1, 21.2-Omega = 3.0.1, master (22 Piers) = 3.0.2 - ALL declare backwards-compatibility abi=3.0.0, so <import addon='xbmc.python' version='3.0.0'/> installs on every one of 19/20/21/22. Declaring 3.0.1 is the only way to hard-gate out Kodi 19. ListItem.setInfo() is DEPRECATED but still present in master (xbmc/interfaces/legacy/ListItem.cpp line 375) - it logs LOGWARNING 'Setting most video/music/picture/game properties through ListItem.setInfo() is deprecated and might be removed in future Kodi versions.' It has NOT been removed in 21 or 22. Also deprecated with warnings: setUniqueIDs, setRating, addSeason, setCast, getUniqueID, getRating, getVotes, and the ListItem.setProperty()/getProperty() keys 'totaltime' and 'resumetime' (use InfoTagVideo.setResumePoint()/getResumeTime()/getResumeTimeTotal()). TYPE STRICTNESS: setInfo parses values via strtol on a string, so a float like 1234.5 was silently truncated; the typed SWIG setters take real C++ ints - InfoTagVideo::setDuration(int) (seconds), setYear(int), setEpisode(int), setSeason(int), setPlaycount(int), setUserRating(int), setRating(float rating, int votes,...), setResumePoint(double time, double totaltime=0.0). Passing a Python float to an int-typed setter raises TypeError, converting an existing silent bug into a hard crash. PERFORMANCE: every ListItem accessor in ListItem.cpp is wrapped in XBMCAddonUtils::GuiLock(languageHook, m_offscreen) - 35 occurrences - so ListItem(offscreen=True) skips the GUI lock. Kodi docs say plugins normally create list items offscreen and add them later, and to use offscreen=False only when managing the container yourself.
